articles.title: Hunger surges in Haiti as gang violence, high food prices and supercharged El Niño persist
articles.description: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) — Nearly six million people in Haiti are experiencing severe hunger, with almost two million facing emergency conditions, according to a new report released Wednesday. The worsening crisis in the Caribbean country of nearly 12 million people is blamed on a surge in gang violence and displacement, combined with high food and fuel prices and an extreme El Niño weather phenomenon that is threatening food security.

articles.title: Long Island Restaurant Week celebrates 20 years of supporting local restaurants and giving back to the community
articles.description: Fall Long Island Restaurant Week will take place from Nov. 1 to Nov. 8. Long Island Restaurant Week, the tri-annual and award-winning dining promotion, is celebrating a major milestone this fall: 20 years of bringing Long Island restaurants and diners together. Over the past two decades, Long Island Restaurant Week (LIRW) has not only supported the Island’s vibrant restaurant community but has also given back to the community it serves, donating more than $40,000 to local Long Island food banks and charitable organizations. One of the promotion’s primary beneficiaries over the years has been The INN (Interfaith Nutrition Network), a Long Island nonprofit dedicated to assisting those challenged by hunger, homelessness and profound poverty. LIRW is proud to have donated over $10,000 to The INN over the span of the promotion’s lifetime. “Since 2006, The INN has been honored to have been one of the recipients of generous donations from Long Island Restaurant Week,” said Cynthia Sucich, Chief Operating Officer for The INN (Interfaith Nutrition Network). “As a local nonprofit organization whose mission is to serve hungry and homeless Long Islanders, these contributions have helped to support our programs that feed and shelter those in need, in a place where many are unaware of the poverty that plagues local communities. Congratulations on 20 years of Long Island Restaurant Week and thank you for your continued generosity and help raising awareness of food insecurity where we live, work, and raise our families together.” The 20th anniversary of Fall Long Island Restaurant Week will take place from Sunday, November 1 through Sunday, November 8, inviting diners across the Island to celebrate two decades of exceptional dining experiences, outstanding local restaurants and unbeatable prix fixe values. Throughout the week, participating restaurants may offer a $25 two-course lunch, a $30 three-course dinner menu, a $40 three-course dinner menu, and/or a $48 three-course dinner prix fixe. Restaurants may choose to offer one, two or any combination of the four prix fixe options during the promotion. Each participating restaurant is required to offer at least three options per course for dinner (appetizer, entrée and dessert) and for lunch (appetizer and entrée or entrée and dessert). Participating restaurants must offer the $25 two-course lunch prix fixe and/or the $30, $40 or $48 three-course dinner prix fixe all night, every night they are open, or during lunch hours, from Sunday through Sunday. On Saturdays, the prix fixe menu may only be offered until 7 p.m. Since its inception, Long Island Restaurant Week has encouraged diners to explore Long Island’s diverse culinary landscape while providing restaurants with an opportunity to welcome new guests and reconnect with longtime customers. This fall, the promotion marks 20 years of celebrating the chefs, restaurateurs and dining destinations that make Long Island a vibrant place to dine. To commemorate the milestone, Long Island Restaurant Week is making its popular Gift Card Giveaway bigger than ever. In honor of 20 years, 20 winners will each receive a $100 gift card to a participating restaurant of their choice, giving diners even more opportunities to experience and support Long Island’s restaurant community. The 20th Anniversary Gift Card Giveaway Sweepstakes begins on Monday, October 26, 2026, at 12:00 a.m. EST and ends on Monday, November 9, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EST. To enter for a chance to win, diners must visit the Long Island Restaurant Week website during the Sweepstakes Period and submit their information through the online entry form. Whether discovering a new neighborhood favorite, returning to a longtime go-to or simply enjoying a great meal at an exceptional value, diners are invited to be part of this milestone celebration and help Long Island Restaurant Week toast to 20 years this fall. For additional information, a list of participating restaurants and menus as they become available, visit www.longislandrestaurantweek.com. “Reaching 20 years is an incredible milestone for Long Island Restaurant Week and a testament to the restaurants and diners who have supported the promotion year after year,” shares Nicole Castillo of Long Island Restaurant & Hospitality Group. “What began as a way to encourage people to dine out and discover new restaurants has grown into a celebration of Long Island’s entire restaurant community. We are especially proud that along the way we have been able to give back to organizations addressing food insecurity right here on Long Island. As we celebrate this anniversary, we look forward to continuing to bring diners and restaurants together for many years to come.” Long Island Restaurant Week is proudly sponsored by Long Island Restaurant News, Discover Long Island & Newsday.

articles.title: Senegal shifts food security funding to domestic budget lines
articles.description: Senegal is shifting toward financial sovereignty in its food security strategy, moving away from a reliance on foreign donors to fund programs aimed at combating malnutrition. Mbaye Sene, Executive Secretary of the National Nutrition Development Council (CNDN), stated that external aid is decreasing, noting that dependency on international partners renders national policy in this sector fragile and unpredictable. To ensure accountability, the government is implementing "budget tagging." This mechanism replaces generalized reporting with targeted transparency, allowing the state to monitor actual expenditures by ministries and reduce the loss of funds before they reach end consumers.
